title: How to Deal with a Charging Bull
short_description: Bulls will generally leave humans alone unless they become angry.

notification.title: How to Deal with a Charging Bull
notification.body: Do not antagonize the bull, and do not move.

content.headline: Do not antagonize the bull, and do not move.
content.text: Do not antagonize the bull, and do not move.
Bulls will generally leave humans alone unless they become angry.

content.headline: Look around for a safe haven—an escape route, cover, or high ground.
content.text: Look around for a safe haven—an escape route, cover, or high ground.
Running away is not likely to help unless you find an open door, a fence to jump, or another safe haven— bulls can easily outrun humans. If you can reach a safe spot, make a run for it.

content.headline: If a safe haven is not available, remove your shirt, hat, or another article of clothing.
content.text: If a safe haven is not available, remove your shirt, hat, or another article of clothing.

Use this to distract the bull. It does not matter what color the clothing is. Despite the colors bullfighters traditionally use, bulls do not naturally head for red— they react to and move toward movement, not color.

content.headline: If the bull charges, remain still and then throw your shirt or hat away from you.
content.text: If the bull charges, remain still and then throw your shirt or hat away from you.
The bull should head toward the object you've thrown.

content.caption: If you cannot find safe cover from a charging bull, remove articles of clothing and throw them away from your body. The bull will veer and head toward the moving objects.

content.text: If you encounter a stampede of bulls or cattle, do not try to distract them. Try to determine where they are headed, and then get out of the way. If you cannot escape, your only option is to run alongside the stampede to avoid getting trampled. Bulls are not like horses, and will not avoid you if you lie down—so keep moving.

full_text:
Do not antagonize the bull, and do not move.
Bulls will generally leave humans alone unless they become angry.
Look around for a safe haven—an escape route, cover, or high ground.
Running away is not likely to help unless you find an open door, a fence to jump, or another safe haven— bulls can easily outrun humans. If you can reach a safe spot, make a run for it.
If a safe haven is not available, remove your shirt, hat, or another article of clothing.
Use this to distract the bull. It does not matter what color the clothing is. Despite the colors bullfighters traditionally use, bulls do not naturally head for red— they react to and move toward movement, not color.
If the bull charges, remain still and then throw your shirt or hat away from you.
The bull should head toward the object you've thrown.
If You Encounter a Stampede
If you encounter a stampede of bulls or cattle, do not try to distract them. Try to determine where they are headed, and then get out of the way. If you cannot escape, your only option is to run alongside the stampede to avoid getting trampled. Bulls are not like horses, and will not avoid you if you lie down—so keep moving.
